tools.name: resolve_country
tools.description: Turns a country name, alias or code (English, Japanese, Chinese) into ISO codes: matches[] {iso2, iso3, name, score}, best first, max 5, empty if none. Call it first when you only have a name: get_country_facts, check_entry_requirements, get_trip_brief and the other tools take ISO codes. Exact, pref

tools.name: get_country_facts
tools.description: Several cited facts for one country in one call: power, currency, emergency numbers, driving side, this year's public holidays, tipping (data.<category>.<field>; a category without data is {}). Use it for a country overview. For one topic use get_emergency_numbers, get_tipping_norms, get_public_holi

tools.name: check_power_compatibility
tools.description: Does a traveller need a plug adapter or voltage converter? verdict {adapter: not_needed | needed | depends_on_plug, converter: not_needed | usually_not_needed | needed_for_single_voltage_devices | unknown, plug_fit[], frequency_note, guidance}, computed from cited plug, voltage and frequency facts (

tools.name: get_emergency_numbers
tools.description: Emergency numbers for one country: data.numbers.value {police, ambulance, fire, general, all_numbers}. A role without its own number is null: then use general, else all_numbers (in 58 countries only all_numbers is filled). Use it when only these numbers are needed; get_country_facts for several fact

tools.name: get_tipping_norms
tools.description: Tipping customs for one country: data.norms.value {overall_context, situations {<situation>: {expectation, guidance_type, percent_min, percent_max}}}; percentages only where a source states them. Use it for "should I tip, and how much?"; get_country_facts for several facts, get_trip_brief for a whol

tools.name: get_public_holidays
tools.description: National public holidays between two dates: data.holidays[] {date, name} by date, plus one citation per year in data.facts[]. Use it to check travel dates for closures and crowds; get_country_facts has this year's list with other facts, get_trip_brief covers a whole trip. Data spans the current year

tools.name: check_entry_requirements
tools.description: Visa/entry information for a short tourist stay, for a pilot set of passports, from official government sources, with verbatim quotes, official links and a mandatory advisory. Decision support only: never a go/no-go verdict. Returns status (visa_free, visa_free_with_requirements, visa_on_arrival, et

tools.name: get_trip_brief
tools.description: Whole-trip brief for 1-5 destinations: per destination, in order, entry (as check_entry_requirements, if passport given), power verdict from home_country, currency, emergency numbers, driving side, tipping and holidays between from and to. Use it to summarise a trip; for one fact use check_entry_req

tools.name: list_recent_changes
tools.description: Dataset change feed, newest first: data[] {changed_on, fact_id, country, category, change: added | updated | removed, old_value, new_value, source_url}. Use it to refresh caches or alert users when a fact changes, then fetch the current cited value (sources, license, confidence) with the matching to

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "check_entry_requirements" stacks urgency/override words (always, never, mandatory). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
